questions.stem: According to the kinetic particle model, what happens to the particles of a substance when it is heated?

options.text: The particles expand and get larger
The particles move faster and gain kinetic energy

questions.explanation: When a substance is heated, its particles gain kinetic energy and move faster. The particles themselves do not change size or number -- it is their speed and energy that increase.

questions.stem: In which state of matter are particles arranged in a regular pattern and only able to vibrate about fixed positions?
questions.explanation: In a solid, particles are closely packed in a regular arrangement and can only vibrate about fixed positions. They are held in place by strong forces of attraction between particles.
